methodological_rigor.justification: Technology-development study introducing HYDRAC polymeric degraders validated via orthogonal biophysical and biological assays: ROMP-based synthesis with SEC-MALS and SDS-PAGE characterization, SAXS globular morphology with Guinier/Kratky analysis, chymotrypsin Michaelis-Menten proteolysis kinetics, CD spectroscopy plus thermal melts, biotin-streptavidin MYC pull-downs, Cy5.5 uptake assays with endocytosis inhibitor panel, RNA-seq across three cell lines (PC3, A549, MYCCaP), GSEA vs siMYC controls, TMT-based whole proteome analysis via Orbitrap Eclipse, in vivo allograft efficacy (MycCaP n=5/group), and KEAP1/VHL/CRBN degron-swap experiments using isogenic knockouts (HCT116 KEAP1 KO, 293T VHL KO) to validate E3-ligase mechanism. Statistics include one-way ANOVA, Benjamini-Hochberg in GSEA, biological/technical replicates (n>=3). Sample sizes in vivo are modest and sex was restricted to males for the prostate model (justified).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical chemistry/biology study with cell-line and murine allograft data; Oxford LoE 5. Translational relevance is high given the validated undruggable targets (MYC, multi-allele KRAS) and the generalizable nature of the platform (VHL/KEAP1/CRBN degron swaps), but clinical applicability requires extensive PK/PD, toxicology, and delivery optimization not addressed here.

reporting_quality.justification: Animal experiments under Northwestern IACUC protocol IS00023911 with Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary reference. Detailed materials/methods with batch-to-batch characterization (Supplementary Tables 1-4) supports reproducibility of polymer synthesis. Cell line source authentication, mycoplasma testing, antibody catalog numbers, and sequencing core details are reported. No explicit ARRIVE compliance statement in the excerpted text, and deposition of RNA-seq and proteomic datasets is not visible in the reviewed sections.

novelty_literature.justification: Introduces a new class of heterobifunctional degraders (HYDRACs) built from statistical peptide-brush copolymers rather than small-molecule PROTACs or molecular glues. First demonstration of a polymer-based degrader for MYC with four interchangeable degron recruiters (RRRG, VHL, KEAP1, CRBN) and extends to multi-allele KRAS via consensus RAS-binding motifs. Offers a generalizable platform that bypasses the requirement for ligandable pockets on the POI. This is a conceptually distinct expansion of the TPD armamentarium.

writing_presentation.justification: Clearly organized narrative moving from platform concept to MYC proof-of-concept, mechanism, selectivity, in vivo efficacy, and extension to KRAS. Schematic figures and orthogonal assays are logically sequenced; legends are detailed. Methods section is comprehensive with minor repetition (CLSM described twice). Some sentences are dense (polymer chemistry and mass spectrometry) and may benefit from clearer signposting for oncology readership.

key_strengths: Novel peptide-brush polymer platform (HYDRAC) for targeted protein degradation bypassing ligandable pocket requirement
Multi-degron modularity validated via VHL, KEAP1, CRBN recruiters and isogenic KO controls
Orthogonal validation of MYC engagement (CD spectroscopy, biotin pulldown, proteomics, GSEA vs siMYC) and in vivo efficacy in MycCaP allografts
Extension to multiple KRAS alleles (pan-KRAS potential), addressing a major undruggable target
Rigorous polymer characterization (SEC-MALS, SAXS, chymotrypsin stability) and reproducibility across polymer batches
key_concerns: Modest in vivo sample size (n=5/group) with single tumor model and male-only allografts
No explicit ARRIVE checklist or explicit deposition accession for RNA-seq/TMT proteomics visible in reviewed text
Pharmacokinetic, biodistribution, and systemic toxicology profiles of HYDRACs not characterized
Clinical translational path requires formulation and delivery optimization not addressed
chief_reviewer.rationale: Novel, technically rigorous chemistry-biology platform paper with multi-modal validation and two undruggable target demonstrations (MYC, KRAS); tier 1 with minor revisions is appropriate given the conceptual novelty and preclinical evidence depth.
